subjective.unit: Chief Complaint: Trouble with heart, swelling ankles, shortness of breath
subjective.citation_text: Doctor: Hello. Could you tell me your age and gender, and what brings you in today? Patient: I'm a woman, and I'm here because I've been having trouble with my heart. My ankles have been swelling, and I've been having a hard time breathing, especially at night. I had to call an ambulance and was taken to the hospital for heart failure. Doctor: Could you please provide more details about the duration and progression of your swelling and shortness of breath? Have you experienced any other symptoms such as fatigue, chest pain, or palpitations? Additionally, have you been diagnosed with heart failure before, and if so, what medications are you currently taking? Patient: I haven't been diagnosed with heart failure before, but I was told I was in the hospital for it. I was having trouble with my ankles swelling and couldn't get them to go down, even when I was in bed. I had to prop myself up to breathe at night, and I felt really bad. I called 911 because I was having a hard time talking, and they took me to the ER. I was told my blood pressure was really high, like 200 over 90. I try to take my medications, but I might miss a dose now and then. I also eat a lot of salty foods, like salt and vinegar potato chips, which I snack on every day at home. Doctor: Have you been evaluated for kidney function or tested for proteinuria, such as a urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio or a 24-hour urine protein test, since your hospitalization for heart failure? Patient: I don't know if I've had any tests for kidney function or proteinuria since I was in the hospital. I wasn't told about any of those specific tests, but I do know I have some kidney disease, which the doctor mentioned. Doctor: Could you confirm if you were told about any kidney function tests, such as serum creatinine or eGFR, or any urine tests for proteinuria, like the urine albumin-to-creatinine
